title: CHAPTER 5: CULTURE, ART AND LITERATURE OF TELANGANA

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Perini Shivatandavam is an ancient warrior dance form historically patronized during the Kakatiya dynasty, performed by male dancers invoking Lord Shiva.
Telangana features a rich dual literary tradition across both Classical Telugu literature and Deccani Urdu literature.
Handicrafts like Pochampally Ikat textiles, Cheriyal scroll paintings, and Pembarthi sheet metal craft represent the state's artisanal heritage.
Major regional festivals such as Bathukamma and Bonalu reflect the vibrant folk traditions and spiritual culture of Telangana.
The indigenous tribes of Telangana, including the Gonds, Chenchus, Lambadas, and Kolams, contribute significantly to its unique cultural fabric.

blocks.content: Kuchipudi is the classical dance form of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Originating from Kuchipudi village in Krishna district (AP), it is characterized by fast rhythmic footwork, graceful body movements, and elaborate costumes. Bharatanatyam is also popular in Telangana.

Perini Shivatandavam is an ancient classical dance form of Telangana that was revived after centuries of obscurity. It is a vigorous masculine dance performed in honor of Lord Shiva. It originated during the Kakatiya period and was performed before soldiers going to war. The dance was revived by Dr. Nataraja Ramakrishna in the 20th century.

blocks.content: Telangana cuisine is characterized by its spicy flavors, extensive use of tamarind, and unique preparations that differ from Andhra cuisine:

items: Hyderabadi Biryani – World-famous; Dum biryani style; Kacchi Gosht ki Biryani
Haleem – Slow-cooked meat and wheat dish; famous worldwide from Hyderabad; GI-tagged product
Sarva Pindi (Sarapapindi) – Rice flour pancake
Uppindi – Broken rice dish
Jonna Rotte – Sorghum (Jowar) flatbread
Sajja Rotte – Pearl millet flatbread
Gongura Mutton – Made with sorrel leaves
Irani Chai – Tea with buffalo milk and malai; specialty of Hyderabad
Osmania Biscuits – Tea-time biscuit specialty of Hyderabad

blocks.content: Telugu is one of the classical languages of India. Telangana has a rich Telugu literary tradition:

items: Nannaya Bhattaraka – First Telugu poet (11th century); wrote Mahabharata in Telugu
Tikkana Somayaji – Second of the Kavitraya (trio); wrote parts of Mahabharata
Errapragada – Third of Kavitraya; completed Mahabharata in Telugu
Palkuriki Somanatha – Saint-poet; wrote in Dwipada style; devoted to Veerashaiva
Potana – Wrote Maha Bhagavatamu; dedicated to Rama; refused Reddi kings' patronage
